- id: plan-mode
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-plan-mode'
  config:
    section: >
      You are in plan mode. Stay in plan mode until the user approves your plan
      through exit_plan_mode or switches the session mode. Imperative language
      to implement changes means plan the implementation, not execute it. A
      user's conversational agreement — including an answer confirming something
      you asked — approves nothing and does not end plan mode; fold the
      confirmed decision into the plan and submit it through exit_plan_mode.


      Explore first. Use non-mutating reads, searches, static analysis, and
      checks to ground the plan in the actual repository. Do not edit or write
      files, change configuration, run formatters or code generation that
      rewrites tracked files, commit, or otherwise carry out the plan. Prefer
      existing functions and patterns over new machinery.


      The tool catalog stays the same across modes for request-cache stability.
      These plan-mode rules override any later tool description or guidance that
      suggests using mutation tools; those tools remain listed only to keep the
      request shape stable. Do not use todo_write to track this planning phase:
      it tracks implementation after an approved plan, while the plan itself
      belongs in exit_plan_mode.


      Resolve discoverable facts by inspection. Use ask_user_question only for
      user-owned choices or material ambiguity that inspection cannot answer. Do
      not ask the user where code lives or how current behavior works when you
      can find out.


      Make the plan decision-complete: state the goal and success criteria;
      group implementation changes by subsystem; identify public API, schema,
      and data-flow changes; cover edge cases, failure modes, tests, acceptance
      criteria, and explicit assumptions. Keep it concise enough to review but
      detailed enough that another engineer can implement it without making
      design decisions.


      When ready, call exit_plan_mode with the complete plan markdown, starting
      with a # title. Make exit_plan_mode the only and final tool call in that
      assistant response: it presents the plan for approval, and implementation
      begins only in a later step after approval. Do not paste the final plan as
      a plain reply or ask "should I proceed?" through prose or
      ask_user_question. If review rejects it, incorporate the feedback and
      present again. If the review channel is unavailable or aborted, stay in
      plan mode and ask the user to switch modes manually; do not proceed with
      implementation.
  disabled: true

resolvedFindings.title: Shared ledger projection metadata could reveal another coordinator's private ledger IDs
resolvedFindings.before: The workspace state has one ledgerProjection slot. read returned that slot without checking owner, although the item list was owner-filtered. Export A, export B, then read as A could return B's itemIds.
resolvedFindings.after: read returns projection only if both its owner and configured path match the caller. Explicit foreign unit reads are rejected; exported items and current units are independently owner-filtered.

resolvedFindings.boundary: The configured ledgerDocument is a shared project path and contains the last exporting owner's snapshot. An actor with explicit file-read authorization can read that shared file. The fix isolates ledger API state; it does not claim file-level privacy between actors authorized to the same document.

resolvedFindings.title: A correct prefix of a compound factual part could become author repair debt
resolvedFindings.before: unlisted was allowed anywhere in a rejected direct/inference part, even when finding.quote identified only its incorrect suffix. Example: 本例通过19项，全部20项均通过 with finding.quote=全部20项均通过 could incorrectly reject 本例通过19项.
resolvedFindings.after: Each rejected interval is now the uniquely located finding.quote inside its factual part. Every non-whitespace character of unlisted.quote must belong to those rejected intervals. Ambiguous or nonmatching metadata stays with the reviewer. review rechecks the metadata after a coverage update.

Revalidation at review against the final coverage snapshot
Reject headings/hypotheses/error-examples as debt, accept real factual heading, reject stale metadata after coverage becomes supported
Correct prefix is rejected as metadata; actual incorrect suffix proceeds to supplement-ready

resolvedFindings.boundary: The host proves agreement between metadata and recorded factual findings. It does not itself determine whether a reviewer has classified an arbitrary sentence correctly; the independent semantic review and audit remain necessary.

resolvedFindings.title: A successful external ledger write followed by failed host-state persistence could leave a closed document and open host state
resolvedFindings.before: exportLedger wrote ledgerDocument before change committed the host state. If state persistence failed, the generated document could show a revision and closed phase that had never committed.
resolvedFindings.after: Only the new ledger export supplies a rollback list to replaceWithHistory. Each successfully completed write appends an inverse operation with the exact expected written bytes. change reverses those operations on operation, state-backup or state-write errors. Recovery conflicts are reported as AggregateError and never returned as successful closure.

evidence.supports: Ledger export opts into compensation before publishing projection metadata
Expected prior-byte comparison, same-directory staged write and replacement
Record only successful writes; include document, log, rolling document backup and rolling log backup
Host commit followed by error compensation in reverse order, with explicit recovery failure reporting
Export path failure leaves ledger-review and running disposition unchanged; later recovery succeeds
Injected host-state rename failure verifies original host state and all four exported document/history/backup byte sequences, then a successful retry closes

resolvedFindings.boundary: Compensation is in memory and handles catchable errors. No durable multi-file journal exists for process termination or power loss. External concurrent edits can cause the expected-byte recovery check to fail; that condition is explicitly reported, requires reconciliation and is not silently overwritten. The concurrent-edit failure branch was inspected statically but has no separate injected regression in this captured batch.

acceptanceMatrix.requirement: Complete current owned IDs, statuses, revision and evidence
acceptanceMatrix.details: Export uses ledgerSummary(true), so finished items remain included. It emits owner, global ledger revision, status counts, current unit phase/receipt, every stable item ID and status, disposition basis/outcome/checkpoint, evidence path/range/hash, coverage receipt/candidate/goal hashes, origin session/event/hash and timestamp. The test captures a late user request and checks all seven IDs, count, revision, backup and idempotence. Evidence formatting was verified from source; the seven-item test does not individually assert every evidence field.

acceptanceMatrix.requirement: Explicit authorization and model read-only projection
acceptanceMatrix.details: ledgerDocument must be a safe exact coordinator.write path and cannot overlap goals, context evidence, instructions, candidates or receipts. It is removed from all model write scopes and has a specific write-handler rejection. Only the coordinator ledger action can export. The policy's write permission authorizes host generation, not model-authored replacements. Without explicit configuration the legacy narrative remains untouched and host state remains authoritative.

acceptanceMatrix.requirement: Closure remains tied to current evidence and complete decisions
acceptanceMatrix.details: Fresh ledger revision/serial read, current goal/candidate acceptance, authorized actually read context and exact decision coverage remain required. Standalone plans cannot borrow completed status from an unrelated receipt. covered requires a current owned accepted replacing unit. review exports the final dispositions inside the same change operation before a successful return. Captured tests include goal changes, stale closure, late messages and unrelated completion rejection.

acceptanceMatrix.requirement: Generalized numbered error-example labels without weakening source checks
acceptanceMatrix.details: NFKC normalization plus conservative leading Markdown presentation removal supports Arabic/Chinese/fullwidth ordinals, brackets and emphasis around visible error labels. Original bytes remain the coverage/quotation basis. Each error-example still requires a visible local label, actual authorized source quote and contradicts/insufficient relation, then becomes illustrated-error rather than a supported premise. Positive tests cover 12 label forms and replay the three original status/correlation/reverse-implication examples. Negative tests reject negated labels, mere mentions, unlabelled assertions and borrowing a preceding heading's label.

def artifact(path, name):
    raw = path.read_bytes()
    text = raw.decode("utf-8-sig")
    kind, data = "text", text
    if path.suffix == ".json":
        kind, data = "json", json.loads(text)
    elif path.suffix == ".jsonl":
        kind, data = "jsonl", [json.loads(x) for x in text.splitlines() if x.strip()]
    return dict(path=name, kind=kind, originalSha256=sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
                publishedSha256=sha256(encoded(data)).hexdigest(), data=data)


def bundle(run):
    files = [p for p in run.iterdir() if p.is_file()]
    for directory in ("calls", "scores", "requests"):
        if (run / directory).is_dir():
            files += list((run / directory).rglob("*.json"))
    return dict(spec="building-loop-experiment/1", family=run.parent.name, run=run.name,
                artifacts=[artifact(p, p.relative_to(run).as_posix()) for p in sorted(files)])
